title: Multiple Statistical Model Ensemble Predictions of Residual Chlorine in Drinking Water: Applications of Various Deep Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
summary: Original study uses measured water samples from the 90-km Lirima Gravity Flow Scheme in Uganda to model residual chlorine concentration from temperature, pH, conductivity and sample time. It reports field-specific environmental water-quality prediction and compares learned model/ensemble performance. The inference is limited to the sampled scheme and retrospective 70/30 series split; no broader safety outcome is established.

evidence.ai_role: Methods §2.1.3: repeated morning/afternoon samples at several locations, with lab-measured temperature, pH, conductivity, residual chlorine and sampling time; 70/30 training/testing subseries. Results compare 6 deep and 9 ML models; Ens2 explains 74% variance on combined data. Field measurement and validation support a narrow environmental prediction result.
